cases.expected: empty set []
cases.description: The schema requires a string property "name". Providing a JsonNode with a valid string value should result in an empty ValidationMessage set (no errors).

group: Missing required property triggers validation error

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message about missing required property 'name'
cases.description: The schema declares "name" as required. An empty JsonNode should cause validate(JsonNode) to return a set with at least one ValidationMessage indicating the missing required property.

group: Wrong type for property triggers validation error

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message about type mismatch for property 'name'
cases.description: The schema expects "name" to be a string. Supplying a numeric value should cause a type‑validation error to be reported.

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: Calling validate(null) should throw a NullPointerException because the implementation forwards the argument to the overloaded method which expects a non‑null JsonNode.

group: Schema with no constraints accepts any JSON

cases.expected: empty set []
cases.description: When the JsonSchema is created from an empty schema ("{}"), any JsonNode is valid. The method should return an empty ValidationMessage set regardless of the node's content.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message about additional property 'extra' not allowed
cases.description: The schema defines "additionalProperties": false and requires a string property "name". Supplying a JSON object that contains an extra property should cause a validation error about disallowed additional properties.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message that value is not one of the allowed enum values
cases.description: The schema specifies an enum ["red","green","blue"]. Providing a value "yellow" which is not listed should trigger an enum‑validation error.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message about pattern mismatch
cases.description: The schema defines a string pattern "^[A-Z]{3}$" (exactly three uppercase letters). Supplying "ab1" violates the pattern and should be reported.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message that the number is less than the minimum (10)
cases.description: The schema sets "minimum": 10 and "maximum": 20. Providing a number below the minimum should produce a minimum‑violation message.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message that the number exceeds the maximum (20)
cases.description: The same schema as above; providing a number above the maximum should produce a maximum‑violation message.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message about array having fewer items than "minItems": 2
cases.description: The schema defines an array with "minItems": 2 and "uniqueItems": true. Supplying an array with only one element violates the minItems constraint.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message about duplicate items when "uniqueItems" is true
cases.description: Using the same array schema, providing duplicate values violates the uniqueItems rule and should be reported.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message about missing required property 'city' inside 'address'
cases.description: The schema defines a property "address" of type object with a required string property "city". Supplying an empty object for "address" should trigger a missing‑property error for "city".

cases.expected: empty set []
cases.description: The root schema contains a "$ref" to a definition that restricts "color" to the enum ["red","green"]. Providing a valid enum value should validate successfully, confirming that $ref resolution is performed.

cases.expected: non‑empty set with at least two messages: missing required property 'name' and missing required property 'age'
cases.description: The schema requires both "name" (string) and "age" (integer). An empty JSON object should produce two separate validation messages, demonstrating that the validator aggregates all errors.

group: Null node accepted when type is null

cases.expected: empty set []
cases.description: The schema specifies "type": "null". Supplying a JSON null literal (Jackson's NullNode) should be considered valid and result in no validation messages.

cases.expected: empty set []
cases.description: The schema defines "type": "boolean". Providing a proper boolean true should validate without errors.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message about type mismatch (expected boolean)
cases.description: The same boolean schema; providing a JSON string "true" instead of a boolean should trigger a type‑mismatch validation message.

cases.expected: UnsupportedEncodingException
cases.description: The schema contains a $ref with an invalid percent‑encoding ("#%ZZ"). During validation the implementation attempts to URL‑decode the fragment, which throws UnsupportedEncodingException. The exception should propagate (or be wrapped in a RuntimeException) when validate(JsonNode) is invoked.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: Jackson's MissingNode represents a non‑existent node. Passing it as the root to validate(JsonNode) should cause the validator to reject the input and throw IllegalArgumentException because a concrete JSON value is required.

cases.expected: StackOverflowError
cases.description: The schema defines a $ref that points to itself, creating an infinite recursion during schema resolution. Invoking validate(JsonNode) should eventually cause a StackOverflowError.

group: Root node of unexpected type (binary) triggers IllegalArgumentException

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: When the root JsonNode is a BinaryNode (e.g., created via JsonNodeFactory.binaryNode()), the validator does not know how to process binary data for most schemas and should throw IllegalArgumentException.
